hypothesis: E1 calibration: measure the judge's own noise floor and score distribution before tuning any translate prompt, to avoid optimizing a measurement artifact (CLAUDE.md S9 screen-gate lesson)
result: judge is RELIABLE and NOT capped: intra-sample sigma T3=0.18 T2=0.22, verdict spread 1:2 2:5 3:10 4:8 5:5 -- it awards 5/5 to 5 of 30 samples, so the fluency ceiling is real translation quality, not a judge artifact. Score distribution proved a cheaper discriminator than the planned human-prose control. Also uncovered a book-specific normalize defect: Kaplan toc.ncx+nav both unresolvable so 94.9% of segments inherit the book title, making rubric v1.1's front/back-matter fold inert and letting 2/30 untranslated English headings into the body-prose pool (T3 12.8 -> ~13.5 once removed). Story S1.13 filed
